entries.heading: てん【典】
entries.evidence: Actual Daijisen body identifies a grand ceremony and a rule to follow. Nikkoku additionally identifies books recording truths or things to be observed. These independently support the ceremony/rule/text branches alongside actual 辞典, 古典 and 典型 families.
entries.decision: Propose title 'reference texts; rules; ceremony', with compound-specific explanations rather than one English substitution for every word. Preserve canonical 八 radical12 and eight strokes. Use structure-unclassified and only a labelled modern-shape mnemonic; no historical book-on-table origin or phonetic claim is established.
entries.limits: The Jitsu heading returned without its substantive entry; no historical derivation is adopted. A raw web_fetch range returned CSS and navigation, not additional dictionary evidence. The actual simplified Daijisen/Nikkoku sections above were returned.

entries.dictionary: デジタル大辞泉; 精選版 日本国語大辞典; 日本大百科全書
entries.heading: こう‐でん〔カウ‐〕【香典／香奠】
entries.evidence: Actual downloaded Daijisen article at character offsets65329-67196 defines money or goods offered before the deceased in place of incense or flowers and supplies 香典を供える. Nikkoku describes money and food contributing toward funeral costs. Nipponica identifies contemporary money-in-an-envelope practice while acknowledging regional noncash gifts.
entries.decision: Add only necessary 香典こうでん, title 'condolence money; funeral gift', as デン practice with exact 香コウ/典デン records and whole-word family1283090. Explain a funeral condolence gift, usually money; not incense itself or a generic present. Retain 香奠 as an alternate spelling; JMdict's rare-form flag belongs to that spelling, not to the pronunciation or the ordinary 香典 word. Explain 香's incense connection without inventing '典 means money' or a historical substitution rule. Propose 香典を用意しました and 香典を渡しました, each with full kana and English; public attestation directly supplies the separate 供える collocation.
entries.limits: Simplified extraction omitted the Daijisen body despite returning its heading. Raw web_fetch50000-66000 ended mid-body; the separate downloaded article was subsequently read in full after tag stripping. The long funeral-etiquette dictionary includes prescriptions and amounts, none adopted. No universal envelope, denomination, religion or regional-etiquette rules are proposed. Original public HTML stays in control logs, not runtime/Git.
